# Coupons: test prints before buying hardware (generated by `python -m rnd.coupons`)

**Why:** these are the riskiest mechanisms in the design. Most cost only filament; C12–C14 use parts in the Step 1a kit ([M1_BENCH_ARM.md](M1_BENCH_ARM.md)). Print them first and record the measurements below; each result updates the named parameter, and the loop re-runs every check.

**Step-1 coupons (M1 exit criterion 6, Fable review #2 M4): C12 insert pull-out, C13 4-ear flange, C14 drive stub**, plus C9 (the bolt circles C14 needs). Pass numbers come from the repo's load cases (`rnd/coupons.py step1_coupons()`).

**Total:** 315 g, 26.2 h with PrusaSlicer's generic profile ≈ **9.2 h on the P2S** (ESTIMATE).

STLs: `rnd/out/coupons/`.

| Coupon | Material | Generic time (h) | Filament (g) | How to print |

## Step-1 coupons (C12–C14)

### C12: Heat-set insert pull-out (Fable C1 / #2 M4) — 1a (no motor)

**Proves:** what one insert in the arm's print holds when its screw pulls it out of the boss, the ESTIMATE behind every insert-in-pull-out joint left in the arm (seat caps, roll end wall, shoulder web, exit-slot strap, cap rims) and behind the 'before' rows of joints.md.

**Pass:**

- M3 (Ø4.0 × 4.0 and × 6): mean ≥ 1.0 kN, lowest of 3 ≥ 0.8 kN (the 1.0 kN the repo assumed: rnd/joints.py, roll_inline.md). For scale: an M3 tightened to 0.5 N·m already pulls ≈ 833 N
- M4 (Ø5.6 × 5.7 and × 8): mean ≥ 1.5 kN, lowest ≥ 1.2 kN (2 × the 750 N M4 preload the repo tightens to, cartridge_m.FLANGE_LOAD, so a seat cap or strap can take its working load on top)
- torque-out: no insert spins below 2 × its build torque (M3 1.0 N·m, M4 1.2 N·m)
- M5 (Ø6.4 × 10, belt-roll fallback only, roll.PINCH): ≥ 3.0 kN; print it only if `PIP_ROLL_DRIVE=belt` comes back

**Print and test:** Print `C12_insert_pullout` in the arm's material (PETG, print_plan.md), 4 perimeters, flat, insert axes vertical (the pull runs across the layers). Press the inserts with the iron at the filament's print temperature, flush ± 0.1. Test each site: a steel washer (bore = insert OD + 0.5) on the boss top as the clamped part, a screw through it into the insert, pulled through a 5:1 lever (the 300 mm lever stock pivoting on an M5 in the stand, the screw 60 mm from the pivot, a bucket at 300 mm filled with water in 1 L steps: 49 N per litre at the insert). Record the load at failure and the mode (insert out clean / boss split / layers parted); then torque-out on fresh sites with a torque screwdriver.

**Updates:** joints.py M3 pull-out ESTIMATE; roll.py PINCH preload (belt roll); arm.SEAT_SCREW sizes; cartridge_m.CAP insert size; a failing row moves that joint to a through-bolt + nut (as the D24 v2 ears).

| Result | |
|---|---|
| measured | |
| pass / fail | |

### C13: Bolted 4-ear cartridge flange (D24 v2, Neon #2 F2) — 1a (no motor)

**Proves:** the friction μ and the preload retention of the printed flange-to-wall joint that carries every GIM6010 cartridge's torque and tipping (cartridge_m.flange_joint: μ 0.3 PETG on PETG and 30 % preload after creep are ESTIMATEs), the nut pockets' 2.6 mm floor.

**Pass:**

- fresh, 4 × ISO 4762 M4 × 12 at 0.6 N·m (≈ 750 N each): no slip at **16.5 N·m** (1.5 × the 11 N·m GIM6010 peak), 10 × each way, 1 min each (a witness line across flange and plate moves ≤ 0.1 mm at r 48)
- fresh breakaway torque recorded → μ = T_slip / (4 × 0.75 kN × r 48 mm); the model's 43 N·m is μ 0.3 (the 50 kg luggage scale at r 100 reaches 49 N·m; if it does not slip, record > 49)
- tipping: no 0.05 mm feeler enters at any ear under **16.1 N·m** bending (1.5 × the 10.7 N·m direct-stage case, 3 g + the belt pull on the motor bearing; the model opens at 33 N·m with 30 % preload)
- after 72 h at 50 °C on the P2S bed (preload only): no slip at **13 N·m** (the 30 %-retained friction the flange rows assume, 1.18 × the peak); each ear screw's breakaway torque recorded
- one spare ear torqued to 1.2 N·m (2 × the preload): the nut does not pull into its pocket, the pocket floor does not crack

**Print and test:** Print `C13_flange_plate` (the stage wall, elbow ear pattern) and `C13_flange_can` (the can's lip, flange and 8 mm of nose, plus a test-only arm with a load hole at r 100) in the stage walls' and cans' materials (print_plan.md). Clamp the plate to the stand by its 4 corner holes. Torque: plate vertical, arm horizontal, weights or the luggage scale on the load hole (1 kg there = 0.98 N·m). Tipping: plate horizontal, the load hanging from the arm (the moment is F × r). Creep: the assembled pair on the bed at 50 °C for 72 h (as the old C1 hold), then re-test.

**Updates:** cartridge_m.FLANGE_LOAD mu_face, retained; belts.md flange rows; EAR (pocket depth).

| Result | |
|---|---|
| measured | |
| pass / fail | |

### C14: D26 drive stub on the GIM output (Fable #2 M3) — 1a on the bare motor (unpowered) + the dummy output; 1b on the rig

**Proves:** (a) whether the GIM6010-8's output bearing tilts freely enough for the stub to sit between it and the wall-B 6001 (belts.md 'hinged'), its PCD, pilot and thread depth; (b) the 8 × DIN 7984 M3 × 6 + Loctite 243 friction joint at 1.5 × the peak with the belt's side load; (c) the same joint on the real output at the drive's peak.

**Pass:**

- (a) tilt stiffness of the output (secant 0 → 9.8 N·m, the housing's own tilt subtracted) **≤ 18 kN·m/rad** (≈ 5.4 N·m per arcmin), i.e. ≥ 1.8′ of tilt at 9.8 N·m (3.2 mm of spot travel on the optical lever at 3 m; 11 µm on a dial at r 20): then the hinged design stands (fatigue 3.13×). Stiffer: the 0.15 mm swap offset drives the stub to 0.56× (fully rigid), so quote the overhung pinion instead (belts.py STUB_SUPPORT_RULE). Hand model, ESTIMATE
- (a) PCD, pilot Ø and thread depth read to ± 0.1 mm (C9 disc + calipers) into cartridge_m.MOTOR['out_pcd'] and belt_stage.STUB; the thread depth ≥ 4 mm for M3 × 6 under a 1.8 mm counterbore
- (b) on the dummy output: no slip (witness ≤ 0.05 mm at r 17) at **16.5 N·m**, 10 × each way, with a **360 N** radial pull at the flange (the motor bearing's share of the 1158 N shaft load at the peak, belts.md hinged); breakaway of each screw ≥ its build torque after (the model holds 27.2 N·m: μ 0.2 × 8 × 1.0 kN × r 17, 2.47×)
- (c) 1b, on the rig: the drive at its 11 N·m peak against the hard stop, 10 ×: no slip (witness mark)

**Print and test:** (a) Motor housing bolted to the stand's plate, output up, unpowered. The lever stock across the output (4 × M3 is enough here), weights of 1 / 2 / 4 kg hung at r 250 (2.5 / 4.9 / 9.8 N·m, no torque about the axis). Read the tilt on the output flange itself, not on the lever (the 6 mm bar bends millimetres): the optical lever first (a small mirror on the flange, a laser spot on a wall 3 m away, 1′ ≈ 1.75 mm of spot), or a 0.002 mm dial test indicator on the flange rim at r ≈ 20 (near its resolution); the same reading on the housing, subtracted; turn the lever 180° and repeat. Note the free play (tilt at ± 0.5 N·m) separately. (b) The dummy output: the 6061 offcut drilled and tapped through `C14_stub_template` on the measured PCD, in a vise; the lever stock counterbored to leave 1.8 mm under the heads (as the stub flange), 8 × M3 × 6 + 243 at ≈ 0.6 N·m (1.0 kN, K 0.2), cured 24 h; 6.7 kg at r 250 is 16.4 N·m; the radial pull with a ratchet strap and the luggage scale at the hub. (c) On the 1b rig.

**Updates:** belts.py stub support rule (hinged or overhung pinion), cartridge_m.MOTOR out_pcd, belt_stage.STUB pilot; the pinion quote.

## Queued, not defined yet (joints.md; a Step-2 gate)

- printed tube clamped as wave 3 (no sleeves) at 8.8 MPa, 1000 h at 40 °C with a load washer: measures φ, the creep ESTIMATE behind joints.md
- the sleeved C1 joint's moment to gap (pitch hub ↔ tube, yaw flange ↔ tube)
- the 7075-T6 yaw flange's tapped M3 threads (strip vs the 12.9 screw)
- the R17 front stop: a 7075 dog on its block at 3 kN, anodised pair, 100 hits (wear and dent) (W16c; replaces the old stop-bush coupon)
- the inline roll output dowels' slip torque on a seller motor (bonded with Loctite 638)

**Small parts for the coupons:** C12–C14 use the Step 1a kit's inserts, M4 × 12 + washers + nuts, M3 × 6, Loctite 243, the lever stock, the luggage scale, the dial test indicator and the 6061 offcut. Others (≈ $15): Ø3 × 8 dowel pins and Ø6 G25 balls (C4, the head KX44), a 300–400 mm HTD 5M-15 belt (C6), TPU filament (C7).

C9 and C14 (a) need the Step-1a GIM6010-8; C14 (c) needs the Step-1b rig.
